findings.problem: The flag convention says that for a deduction row 'No = removed from the base before the tax', so Yes = not removed. The 42 reversal deduction rows (Wage Type Catalogue rows 2-36 and 38-43: 21100-21213, 21150-21152, housing and transport deductions) carry Yes on N/O/Q1-Q5/Y/Z, while their column D says 'it reduces the same bases as the earning'. Under the declared convention the engine would not reduce the base for a reversal. Pre-tax deductions (401(k), row 46: N=No, Q1=Yes) follow the convention, so one Deduction category carries two opposite readings.
findings.expected: Amend A3 to define two classes explicitly: (1) a reversal deduction carries the flags of the reversed earning, with Yes = the signed amount reduces that base; (2) for a salary-reduction or pre-tax deduction, No = removed from the base before the tax. State the class in column D (or in Category) of each reversal row.
